quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Press yourself against your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, when can you pass?

options.text: If you are on an expressway.

questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you can pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: The broken yellow line side allows passing. The solid yellow line side does not allow passing.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Places where you must always stop.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beams to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your dashboard lights bright so other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions. Steering ability does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space to safely return to the driving lane. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to move back into the right lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed on one-way streets and roads where you cannot enter. You may see this sign if you try to go the wrong way on an expressway ramp.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that roadwork is coming. When you drive through a work zone, watch for temporary traffic control devices.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always demand the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming toward you.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming toward you.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is very close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: Slowing down is the first thing you should do when visibility is poor or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Change your driving if you see this hand signal from a driver ahead of you.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should a driver stop?

options.text: Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop only where you can see at least 200 feet on both sides, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Sound a sharp horn blast if a child or other pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Is it safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. Your tires may lose grip on the road, and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Your body removes approximately:
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one alcoholic drink in one hour. However, how impaired you become depends on many factors, including how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your general health.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is:
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, always yield the right-of-way to people crossing any street.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Enter the far-right traffic lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder of the main road to reach traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up to merge. You should stay stopped while waiting for a safe gap to appear.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Lanes move in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
Lanes move in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Lanes move in the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed yellow line means drivers can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Making a right turn at this sign would be unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll toward the curb, not into traffic.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using the brakes gently.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is immediate danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white backgrounds. They tell drivers what they must or must not do in an area. They may show speed limits, prohibit passing or turning, or explain other driving rules.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren nearby but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane need to merge.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians when driving near schools.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to the direction you came from.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars keep passing you on both sides. What should you do?
questions.explanation: On highways with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. Use the right lane if you are driving slower than traffic around you.

questions.question: What do highways use to help drivers get into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road.
White arrows in the middle of the lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes.
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: How far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop from 55 mph?
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than smaller cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs about 400 feet to stop from 55 mph.
